cd /tmp/eff-reo7ihbe/work; H="Authorization: ApiKey $KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY"
curl -s -H "$H" "$KIBANA_URL/api/dashboards/study-seed-site-health" | python3 -c '
import json,sys,copy
d=json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]
p=copy.deepcopy(d["panels"][1])
p.pop("id");p["config"]["title"]="Requests by host"
p["config"]["layers"][0]["x"]["fields"]=["host.keyword"]
p["grid"]={"x":0,"y":12,"w":24,"h":12}
d["panels"].append(p)
json.dump(d,sys.stdout)' > body.json
curl -s -X PUT -H "$H" -H "kbn-xsrf: true" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "$KIBANA_URL/api/dashboards/study-seed-site-health" -d @body.json | head -c 600; echo
curl -s -H "$H" "$KIBANA_URL/api/data_views/data_view/90943e30-9a47-11e8-b64d-95841ca0b247" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
f=json.load(sys.stdin)["data_view"]["fields"]
print([k for k in f if k.startswith("host")])'
curl -s -H "$H" "$KIBANA_URL/api/alerting/rules/_find?search=Server%20errors" | head -c 800

content.text:
Both changes are made, and I checked each one by reading it back from Kibana.

1. **Dashboard:** I added a third panel, "Requests by host", to the existing "Site health" dashboard. It's a bar chart of request counts by `host.keyword` on the Kibana Sample Data Logs data view. It sits below the other two panels, and they're unchanged.
2. **Rule:** I enabled the existing "Server errors" rule. It now shows as enabled.

I created no new dashboards or rules.
